fea.note: HUBB_Ah on the adopted shape (seats at Y 298.86, R 4 at the tubes), Intel direct sparse. The lowest of the hub-top regions on the run with a 1.3 mm zone on the six tube-to-plate rounds (383k nodes): von Mises and layer tension round the cable tunnel, shear at the rounds. Standard mesh (338k nodes): 1.95 in shear at the rounds, within 6 % on the 0.5 mm ball and 1 % on the 1 mm ball (2.07 against 2.06). Left out as a connector artefact: the tube walls within 3 mm of the head seats, where the screws are tied rigidly (shear 1.40 to 1.47)

HUBL_G90YAWP_MAX on the adopted shape, 1.20 M nodes; 1.55 is the governing figure (shear across the layers at the lug), entered as bulk; von Mises 2.66. Not repeated on a second mesh for this shape: the lugs are those of rev D3c7, whose mesh study is in A_HUB_LUGS.md, and the figure moved by 0.01 across the four rev E1 shapes
HUBL_STOP6_ZB on the adopted shape, 1.20 M nodes; 3.11 is shear across the layers, entered as bulk; von Mises 5.44. Not repeated on a second mesh

access.method: by geometry, not a ray check: the six M4 heads sit on the tube ends in the open centre bore and take a straight driver from the arm side before the arm goes on; the arm thread compared the first rev E1 export with the released hub below Y 302 (identical) and checked its cable route (3.64 mm smallest clearance)
access.notes: M4 x 30 with one washer goes 5.2 mm into the RS02; its holes bottom out at 6.5 to 7 mm (Joey, measured 2026-11-15)
